1.The Maritime Safety Authority of Fiji (MSAF) notes in past marine incidents the need for crew familiarization with shipboard equipment and systems.
2.This Marine Notice wishes to make recommendations to all Shipowners & operators having large fleets for the need to establish dedicated onshore or fleet-based training workshops specifically for crew trainings and practices. These workshops will boost crew familiarity, hands-on safety drill practice, and operational readiness for onboard equipment and systems.
3.Be advised that the Maritime Transport Act 2013 and the Maritime (STCW Convention) Regulations 2014 highlights the need for crew familiarization with critical shipboard equipment, bridge systems, safety gear, and emergency appliances through continuous practical training as it would enhance maritime safety and the protection of the marine environment.
4.For any clarification, please contact the undersigned.
SAVENACA CAVALEVU
EXECUTIVE CHAIRMAN (MSAF)
Maritime Safety Authority of Fiji
22nd October 2026

1.This Marine Notice serves to remind all Shipowners, Ship Operators, Masters, Seafarers and Agents of the importance of maintaining order and discipline of all persons on board ships to protect safety of life at sea and ensure lawful crew management.
2.With recent cases on the above subject matter, the Maritime Safety Authority of Fiji (MSAF) would like to remind all Shipowners, Ship Operators, Masters, Seafarers and Agents of the Master’s duty to have the final authority to control the ship while in command and for the discipline of all persons on board.
3.Additionally, Shipowners, Ship Operators, Masters, Seafarers and Agents are reminded to ensure that disciplinary procedures are implemented as part of the Safe Ship Management System for the Company and also onboard its ships.
4.This Notice serves to give notice that any misconduct affecting the safe operation of the ships, repeated disregard of lawful safety requirements or instructions, or misconduct contributing to any accident, incident or mishap should be reported to the MSAF. Any such recurring records against a seafarer will engage the enforcement measures of MSAF.
5.Reporting of any disciplinary issues to the above notice is to be addressed to:
The Chief Executive Officer
Maritime Safety Authority of Fiji
Level 4 Kadavu House,
414 Victoria Parade
SUVA
For any clarification, please contact MSAF on +679 3315266.
SAVENACA CAVALEVU
EXECUTIVE CHAIRMAN
Maritime Safety Authority of Fiji
29th October 2026

The Maritime Safety Authority of Fiji (MSAF) wishes to advise all shipowners, ship operators, Masters and Maritime stakeholders of the servicing facility currently approved by the Authority to undertake the servicing of inflatable liferafts in Fiji.
This Marine Notice is issued to ensure that inflatable liferafts carried on vessels are serviced by an MSAF-approved servicing station and within the approved scope of the facility.
Approved Liferaft Servicing Station
Facility: Liferaft Sales and Service Centre (Fiji) Pte Limited.
Location: Corner of Renown Street and Rodwell Road, Suva.
MSAF Statement of Compliance: LRSC 01/2026.
The facility has been assessed and approved by MSAF in accordance with regulation 10.4 Paragraph 10 of the Maritime (Fiji Maritime Code) Regulations 2014.
2.Approved Liferaft Brands.
1)Shanghai Liferaft Brands
2)SEA-AIR-Ningbo Neptune Life Saving Equipment Co. Ltd
3)Cun Hong-Shanghai Cunhong Marine Lifesaving Appliances Co. Ltd
4)HYF/HUAYANG-Yantai Huayang Lifesaving Equipment Manufacturing Co. Ltd
The specific Liferaft types and models covered by the facility approval are provided in Appendix A to this Marine Notice.
Advice to Shipowners and Operators
•Ensure liferaft are serviced at the required intervals.
•Ensure servicing is undertaken by an MSAF-approved servicing station.
•Confirm that the servicing station is authorised to service the particular make, type and model of liferaft presented.
•Retain servicing documentation and make it available during MSAF surveys and inspections.
•Do not accept servicing or certification of liferaft that fall outside the approved scope of the servicing station.
Where a liferaft make or model is not listed in Appendix A, shipowners and operators are advised to contact MSAF before making servicing arrangements. MSAF will advise the maritime industry through appropriate notices should additional servicing stations or liferaft brands be approved.
For further information or clarification, please contact the Ships Inspection Department, Maritime
Safety Authority of Fiji. Phone 3315266
Issued by:
Savenaca Cavalevu.
for Chief Executive Officer.
